title: sorted() vs sort()
prompt: scores = [7, 10, 8] is given. Print the sorted version WITHOUT changing scores, then print scores unchanged on the second line.

tests.name: original untouched
tests.code:
assert len(printed) == 2, f"expected two lines, got {printed}"
assert "10" in printed[0] and "7" in printed[0], f"first line should be sorted, got {printed[0]}"
assert printed[1].strip().startswith("[7, 10"), f"second line must be the original order, got {printed[1]}"
tests.hint: print(sorted(scores)) then print(scores) — sorted() leaves the original alone.
